title: Tilenus: primarily in intellect, secondarily in will as it moves it
source_text: V. Sic rem istam explicat Tilenus, Disputatione de Fide justificante: Fides, inquit, est in intellectu primò per se, & proprie; in voluntate secundariò, nempe συναπτικῶς, quatenus eam movet & afficit. Sicut scientia, qua bonum a malo internoscimus, subjective inest menti, voluntati effective, quum elicit, aut imperat actiones quas ratio dictat.
pass_a_gloss: So Tilenus explains the matter in his Disputation on Justifying Faith: Faith, he says, is in the intellect first of all by itself and properly; in the will secondarily, namely synaptically, insofar as it moves and affects it. Just as the knowledge by which we distinguish good from evil is subjectively in the mind, yet effectively in the will when it elicits or commands the actions that reason dictates.
pass_b_english: Tilenus: faith primarily and properly in intellect; secondarily in will as mover.
Like moral knowledge: subjective in mind, effective in will when it commands action.
